title: KLA Revenue Jumps 29 Percent as AI Demand Lifts Chip Equipment Market Toward 2027
excerpt: KLA beat estimates with $4.14 billion in quarterly revenue and guided higher, as Gartner forecasts semiconductor sales approaching $1.94 trillion in 2027.
body:
• KLA reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $4.14 billion, up 28.9% year over year, with non-GAAP earnings of $1.22 per share beating estimates as AI infrastructure spending lifted wafer inspection sales 37%.
  • KLA guided second-quarter revenue to $4.7 billion, plus or minus $200 million, and raised its 2026 wafer equipment market outlook to the mid-$150 billion range, expecting it to exceed $200 billion in 2027.
  • Gartner forecasts global semiconductor revenue of $1.94 trillion in 2027, including $1.08 trillion from memory, with AI spending reaching $3.64 trillion.
  • For investors, the test in 2027 shifts from demand to returns: whether AI spending converts into earnings at equipment makers, memory suppliers and cloud platforms.

KLA Corporation reported record September-quarter results driven by artificial intelligence infrastructure investment, as demand for process-control equipment rose across leading-edge foundry, logic, memory and advanced packaging. Revenue increased 28.9% year over year to $4.14 billion, according to Zacks, while non-GAAP earnings rose 38.6% to $1.22 per share.

Inspection demand leads the quarter

Semiconductor Process Control revenue reached $3.75 billion, accounting for 91% of total revenue and growing 29% year over year. Wafer Inspection remained the largest product category at $2.11 billion, or 51% of revenue, up 37% year over year and 19% sequentially. Patterning revenue grew 29% to $862 million, and services revenue advanced 14% to $850 million on a larger installed base.

Foundry and logic represented 72% of Semiconductor Process Control systems revenue from semiconductor customers, with memory at 28%, supported by advanced DRAM and high-bandwidth memory demand. Geographically, China contributed 34% of revenue, followed by Taiwan at 25% and North America at 15%. Non-GAAP gross margin was 62.7%, and operating margin expanded 240 basis points sequentially to a record 46.1%, even as management cited elevated memory component costs as a headwind.

A larger equipment market in 2027

KLA expects advanced packaging process control revenue to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, growth of more than 70% year over year. For the December quarter, the company guided revenue to $4.7 billion, plus or minus $200 million, with non-GAAP earnings of $1.44 per share, plus or minus 11 cents. Memory is expected to rise to 40% of systems revenue in that quarter, with DRAM at 84% of memory and NAND at 16%.

The company also raised its calendar 2026 wafer equipment market outlook, including advanced packaging, to the mid-$150 billion range and expects the market to exceed $200 billion in calendar 2027. Second-half 2026 revenue is expected to grow about 25% over the first half, supported by backlog and supply capacity.

The 2027 outlook beyond one company

The broader forecasts point in the same direction. Gartner expects worldwide AI spending of $2.67 trillion in 2026, rising to $3.64 trillion in 2027, with AI infrastructure accounting for about $1.98 trillion, according to Zacks' 2027 outlook. Gartner puts global semiconductor revenue at $1.56 trillion in 2026 and $1.94 trillion in 2027, including $1.08 trillion from memory. SEMI separately expects global 300mm fab equipment spending to rise 14% to $151 billion in 2027.

What to watch

Investors will watch whether that spending produces measurable returns. Higher financing costs, supply constraints and capital efficiency will test the cycle in 2027, even as enterprise adoption, inference demand and AI agents add new workloads. For equipment makers such as KLA and memory suppliers, the next quarters will show whether process-control intensity and high-bandwidth memory demand keep rising faster than the wider semiconductor market.
